# Colors

<!-- Generated by scripts/core_docs.py; edit the source of truth and regenerate. -->

Import `Color` and `colors` from `openbacktesting`. Colors are immutable RGBA values used by plotting and color inputs.

[Color](#openbacktesting-color)

```python
from openbacktesting import Color, colors

up = colors.GREEN
faded = up.with_transparency(80)
custom = Color.rgb(30, 120, 220, transparency=25)
parsed = Color.from_hex("#2277AA")
print(custom.to_hex())

middle = Color.from_gradient(
    50, lower=0, upper=100, lower_color=colors.RED, upper_color=colors.GREEN,
)
print(middle.to_hex())
```

`rgb` takes integer red/green/blue components in `0..255`. Transparency is `0..100`: zero is opaque, 100 is invisible. `from_hex` accepts only `#RRGGBB` or `#RRGGBBAA`; the alpha byte uses 255 for opaque. `to_hex()` returns uppercase `#RRGGBBAA` for saving or passing to another application.

`from_gradient(value, lower, upper, lower_color, upper_color)` is called with keyword bounds/colors as shown above. It interpolates RGBA components and clamps values outside the bounds. Bounds must be finite and strictly increasing; endpoint colors must be `Color` values. Convert NumPy/indicator scalars with `float(...)` after checking validity.

Use `self.plotting.line(self.average, color=faded)` for a static color, or compute a scalar gradient in `next()` and pass it to `self.plotting.bar_color(...)`. Color arrays are not accepted. For a user setting, declare `inputs.color(colors.TEAL, title="Line color")`; the runtime value is a Color.

<!-- API: openbacktesting.Color -->

## Color

```python
Color(red, green, blue, alpha=255)
```

Immutable color compared by all four channels; alpha means opacity, with no implicit equality to strings.

| Attribute | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <a id="openbacktesting-color-red"></a><!-- API: openbacktesting.Color.red -->`red` | `int` | Red byte from 0 to 255. |
| <a id="openbacktesting-color-green"></a><!-- API: openbacktesting.Color.green -->`green` | `int` | Green byte from 0 to 255. |
| <a id="openbacktesting-color-blue"></a><!-- API: openbacktesting.Color.blue -->`blue` | `int` | Blue byte from 0 to 255. |
| <a id="openbacktesting-color-alpha"></a><!-- API: openbacktesting.Color.alpha -->`alpha` | `int` | Opacity byte: 0 is transparent and 255 is opaque. |

### Attributes

| Attribute | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| <a id="openbacktesting-color-transparency"></a><!-- API: openbacktesting.Color.transparency -->`transparency` | 0–100 transparency derived from quantized alpha; it may differ from the original percentage. |

<a id="openbacktesting-color-from-hex"></a>

<!-- API: openbacktesting.Color.from_hex -->

### Color.from_hex

```python
Color.from_hex(value)
```

Parse six- or eight-digit hexadecimal colors; append FF for six digits.

<a id="openbacktesting-color-rgb"></a>

<!-- API: openbacktesting.Color.rgb -->

### Color.rgb

```python
Color.rgb(red, green, blue, *, transparency=0)
```

Construct from integer RGB and 0–100 transparency; 0 is opaque, 100 is fully transparent.

<a id="openbacktesting-color-with-transparency"></a>

<!-- API: openbacktesting.Color.with_transparency -->

### Color.with_transparency

```python
Color.with_transparency(transparency)
```

Replace alpha using 0–100 transparency and return a new value; do not modify or multiply the original color.

<a id="openbacktesting-color-to-hex"></a>

<!-- API: openbacktesting.Color.to_hex -->

### Color.to_hex

```python
Color.to_hex()
```

Return uppercase #RRGGBBAA; fully transparent colors retain RGB and do not become None.

<a id="openbacktesting-color-from-gradient"></a>

<!-- API: openbacktesting.Color.from_gradient -->

### Color.from_gradient

```python
Color.from_gradient(value, *, lower, upper, lower_color, upper_color)
```

Linearly interpolate a scalar between unpremultiplied RGBA bytes at both endpoints; clamp outside the interval.
